items.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
items.content:
Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia

Nov. 23, 2026, 8:59 AM EST  /  Updated   Nov. 23, 2026, 4:34 PM EST

By Steve Kopack , Daniel Arkin and Jared Perlo

Jensen Huang will return as Nvidia’s president and CEO, the company’s board announced Monday, in a stunning reversal for an executive who resigned two weeks ago following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy.

The move is effective immediately, the chip giant said in a statement. The company said the board’s unanimous decision to reinstate Huang came after “input from senior levels of the United States government.”

President Donald Trump cheered news of Huang’s return in an interview with CNBC and confirmed that he personally intervened to make it happen, speaking “directly and indirectly” with the company’s board — a highly unusual step for an American president. He said he believed the executive “did nothing wrong” and “there’s nothing wrong with a comeback.”

In a previous social media post, Trump said the federal government had “no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”

Nvidia’s stock soared 31% on the news, buoying the market after a technology sell-off Friday that seemed to confirm anxieties about a bubble in the AI sector. Nvidia’s advanced computer chips power key AI firms’ models, and the company has helped finance the country’s massive investment in new data centers.

Huang said in a statement of his own that he was “honored to return to NVIDIA.”

Huang has established himself in recent years as the unofficial ambassador for the AI boom, the companies backing it and the trillions of dollars being poured into the sector. Nvidia employees greeted him with loud cheers at the company’s corporate headquarters in Santa Clara, California, on Monday, videos posted online showed.

“I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang said in his statement.

The reinstatement was all the more dramatic given that Nvidia’s newly installed chairman, Harvey Jones, effectively dismissed this possibility last week. “The Nvidia Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said in a statement on Nov. 17.

In an interview the same day, Nvidia’s interim chief executive Collette Kress also said that the company would not reinstall Huang.

Huang’s removal from Nvidia came after The New York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies believed was a Chinese spy. The Financial Times followed that report, saying that Huang had an affair with the woman.

In a memo to Nvidia’s workforce Nov. 8, Huang said, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

The New York Times then reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with a senior leader at Nvidia who reported directly to him.

The company’s board launched a search for a new leader, reportedly seeking out Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas. However, Haas earlier Monday announced that he was remaining at Arm, with a contract extension through 2033.

Nvidia also set up a new “national security and export control oversight” panel in light of the revelations about Huang.

Trump, in his social media post, said Attorney General Todd Blanche “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”

Blanche spoke with Trump over the weekend and told him that the Justice Department had no evidence of any wrongdoing by either Huang or Nvidia, a Justice Department official told NBC News.

Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, who serves on the Senate Foreign Relations and Intelligence committees, expressed skepticism about Trump’s assurances. “No national security risk? Based on what?”…

items.title: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit
items.content:
Artist's impression of the two BepiColombo orbiters, which will use a host of instruments to unravel Mercury's mysteries. Photograph: Esa/PA

Artist's impression of the two BepiColombo orbiters, which will use a host of instruments to unravel Mercury's mysteries. Photograph: Esa/PA

Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit

BepiColombo double probe will map planet’s surface and study its interior to shed light on its unusually large core

After a voyage of more than eight years and 6bn miles, a joint European-Japanese space mission has arrived at Mercury and is preparing to swing into orbit around the tiny, barely explored world.

The BepiColombo mission will become only the second in history to circle the first rock from the sun and the smallest planet in the solar system when flight controllers fire the spacecraft’s thrusters on Saturday and send it into orbit.

For researchers, the €1.6bn (£1.4bn) mission is the best hope yet of understanding how Mercury formed so close to the sun, why it has a magnetic field, and what makes up the frozen ice that lurks in the planet’s permanently shadowed craters.

“We’re very excited, it’s been a long wait,” said Prof Emma Bunce at the University of Leicester, who has worked on the project for 20 years.

Getting to Mercury poses unusual difficulties. Because the planet is near the centre of the solar system, spacecraft accelerate under the sun’s gravity and must spend much of their time braking to avoid shooting straight past. “It’s a very complex and challenging mission,” said Bunce, the principal investigator on an instrument called the Mercury Imaging X-ray Spectrometer, or MIXS, which will analyse the geochemical composition of the planet’s surface.

A photo made available by the European Space Agency in October 2021 shows a view of Mercury captured by the BepiColombo mission. Photograph: European Space Agency/AFP/Getty Images It will be some months before scientists can start observing Mercury. In early December, the spacecraft will separate into two orbiters, one European, the other Japanese, which will manoeuvre to different polar orbits around the planet. Science operations are due to start in April next year.

The European probe, named the Mercury Planetary Orbiter or MPO, will map the planet’s surface and composition at high resolution, and study Mercury’s interior to shed light on its unusually large core. Its Japanese partner will measure the planet’s magnetic field and its sodium exosphere, the extremely thin layer of gas and atoms that surrounds the planet. Mercury is only 50% larger than the moon but has four times its mass. One question the mission will explore is why the rock is so dense.

Prof Geraint Jones, the lead project scientist on BepiColombo at the European Space Agency, said anticipation of the scientific results had kept everyone enthused during the spacecraft’s eight-year journey .

“We’re expecting to learn a huge amount, bringing more powerful instruments on two spacecraft to study all aspects of the planet – its interior, surface, and the space around it,” he said.

Mercury is a planet of extremes. The tiny world takes 58 Earth days to rotate on its axis, meaning any given spot on the surface can experience daylight for three months and then night-time for three months. It is little more than a third of Earth’s distance from the sun, at only 36m miles. In the day, ground temperatures reach 450C while at night they drop to -180C.

Jones said: “As well as cameras covering a wide range of wavelengths to study the surface, we’ll be ‘tasting’ the gases around the planet, sensing the magnetic field, probing the interior with ultrasensitive instruments, and mapping the shape of the whole planet with a laser.”

The spacecraft are expected to orbit Mercury for about three years, after which they will run out of fuel, lose altitude and ultimately slam into the surface. “Sadly, they are not coming back,” said Bunce.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: Want clean power for data centers? Try giant heat batteries.
items.content:
Data center developers are scrambling to find enough electricity to power their energy-intensive facilities. Some are building their own fossil gas power plants. But that comes with tradeoffs — sky-high equipment costs, yearslong waits for backlogged turbines, and growing public backlash against their polluting plans.

A  new report from think tank Energy Innovation proposes a faster, cheaper, and cleaner route for powering off-grid data centers: giant heat batteries that are fueled by low-cost solar and wind.

This ​ “ hybrid thermal power” approach can be cost-competitive with fossil gas in many parts of the country, said Eric Gimon, the report’s author and an Energy Innovation senior fellow. Even more important, it can deliver power within a year or two in places where renewable energy is under development, he said — much faster than the wait for a gas plant.

“ It’s a pretty simple solution that hyperscalers and developers can pursue,” Gimon said. ​ “ You can do off-grid that’s fast, clean, reliable, and affordable.”

Nevertheless, Gimon said he’s unaware of a U.S. data center taking this approach today. That’s despite the availability of heat batteries from a number of different companies, including  Antora ,  Brenmiller Energy ,  Electrified Thermal Solutions , and  Rondo Energy .

These energy storage systems use electricity to heat rocks, bricks, or other materials to temperatures exceeding 1 , 000 degrees Celsius ( 1 , 832 degrees Fahrenheit). The systems can retain that heat for hours, days, or even weeks at a time, and then dispatch it later.

Most thermal storage systems installed today supply industrial process heat for everything from food processing to cement production. But they can also use that heat to boil water, spin a steam turbine, and produce electricity.

Storing heat to make electricity has its drawbacks. The process recovers only about 40 % of the total energy that’s been put into it, mainly because of losses in converting heat to steam and then to power, Gimon said. That’s not great, compared with the typical low-to-mid- 90 % ​ “ round-trip efficiency” rate for lithium-ion batteries.

“ But when I started modeling it, I realized TES [thermal energy storage] is cost-effective,” he said.

Data centers that want to run independently of the grid and on clean energy will need to store enormous amounts of power for when solar and wind aren’t available. As long as the solar and wind power is cheap enough, and the value of the electricity being generated from the steam turbines is high enough, the efficiency losses are tolerable. In fact, thermal batteries would be cheaper than conventional lithium-ion storage over longer durations, Gimon said.

Gimon also looked at how fossil-fueled boilers could run on fuel stored on-site, to give the thermal storage and gas turbines emergency backup power, much like data centers rely on emergency backup diesel generators today. This graphic shows how all the pieces fit together.

All told, Gimon estimated that these ​ “ hybrid thermal power brick” systems can deliver reliable, round-the-clock power at a cost of about $ 120 per megawatt-hour — a figure that includes the cost of developing the renewables that deliver their primary power.

Depending on where a data center is located, that can be competitive with building a dedicated gas-fired power plant. References range from about  $ 72 per MWh for a data center in West Texas to the $ 140 to $ 165 per MWh that  investment bank Jeffries estimated Meta is paying for an off-grid gas power plant in Ohio.

But for large data center developers, ​ “ the issue right now isn’t so much cost, but speed to power,” Gimon said. items.content:
Firefox 161 Brings Per-Site VPN Toggling, Classic Themes Section

Written by Michael Larabel in Mozilla on 23 November 2026 at 09:11 AM EST. 8 Comments

Mozilla Firefox 161 release binaries are now available for this newest bi-weekly feature release to this open-source web browser.

Firefox 161 for developers adds support for the random() CSS function, support for nested arbitrary substitution functions, and support for the CSS Typed Object Model.

Firefox 161 adds the ability to create a shortcut now for easily copying the current tab's URL. By default no shortcut is assigned by default but from the shortcuts area is the ability to add a key combination if frequently wanting to copy the current tab's URL.

There is also now a "classic themes" section in the themes area of Firefox. The classic themes section includes the likes of the older Proton theme from prior Firefox versions, a Firefox OLED theme, and more.

Firefox's built-in VPN also now allows turning it on or off for specific sites. This is a convenient helper if wanting to only use their VPN service when accessing certain sites or using it everywhere except for excluding it from select sites.

The Firefox 161 release binaries and more details on this new version via ftp.mozilla.org .
